title: Laredo man gets 10 years' probation for assaulting man over $100 debt
excerpt: Valentin Vasquez pleaded guilty to aggravated assault and was sentenced to 10 years in prison, probated for 10 years, in the September 2024 pistol assault of a man who was said to owe $100.
content:
A Laredo man was sentenced to 10 years in prison, probated for 10 years, after pleading guilty to aggravated assault in a 2024 case in which a man was struck in the face with handguns over a reported $100 debt, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

Valentin Vasquez pleaded guilty Sept. 29 to aggravated assault, with no deadly-weapon finding, and was sentenced Oct. 29 under a plea agreement, the Morning Times reported. The sentence also includes 200 hours of community service, anger-management classes and other conditions. Judge Monica Z. Notzon of the 111th District Court sentenced Vasquez, who had originally faced aggravated assault causing serious bodily injury, a second-degree felony punishable by two to 20 years in prison.

According to a police affidavit, Laredo police responded at about 5:03 a.m. on Sept. 15, 2024, to the 3300 block of Cedar Avenue and found a woman's boyfriend bleeding from his right eyebrow. The affidavit states the woman was watching movies when she asked the man if he had vandalized a vehicle; the man texted two others, who arrived and began hitting the boyfriend in the face with handguns. One of the suspects said the boyfriend owed $100, and another pointed a gun at the woman and tried to take her cellphone, according to the affidavit.

Co-defendant Tommy Adrian Vasquez, 20, also faces aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, a second-degree felony, according to the Morning Times. He waived arraignment through attorney Joe Rubio, did not appear Sept. 1, and his case is set for an informal pretrial Nov. 9, a pretrial Dec. 1, a final pretrial Jan. 20 and jury selection Feb. 8.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, November 9, 2026.
